title: Learning classifies severe paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration
summary: XGBoost classified severe multifidus fatty infiltration in a retrospective 316-patient lumbar-surgery cohort, using MRI-defined infiltration as the reference. Internal validation reported AUC 0.87, with age, sex and facet degeneration prominent among model features. Pre-split imputation and feature ranking can inflate performance; these cross-sectional associations do not show causes, future deterioration or improved surgical outcomes.
ai_technology: XGBoost; random-forest feature ranking and imputation
organization: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Hospital for Special Surgery; University Hospital Ulm

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Recorded preoperative characteristics compared with MRI-defined severe muscle fatty infiltration using a 70:30 internal patient split.
evidence.unknown: Independent clinical utility and causal direction remain unestablished; preprocessing/feature ranking before partitioning and the surgical-only population constrain interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient-boosted trees learn clinical/imaging associations with severe fatty infiltration, allowing classification and exploratory feature ranking.
